content: Meperidine, also known by street names such as Demmies, Mapergan, or Pethidine, is a medication prescribed to alleviate moderate to severe pain. It belongs to a class of drugs called narcotic analgesics, which are similar to morphine. Meperidine works by altering the way the body perceives pain. Meperidine is available in tablet and liquid (syrup) forms for oral administration. It is typically taken every 3 to 4 hours as needed for pain, with or without food. It is crucial to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take meperidine exactly as directed. Swallow the tablets whole without splitting, chewing, or crushing them. Crushing, chewing, snorting, or injecting meperidine can lead to severe side effects or death, especially in individuals who are dependent on or abusing the medication. If you are using the syrup form, mix your dose with half a glass of water before swallowing to avoid numbing of the mouth. Your doctor may adjust your dose during treatment based on your pain levels and any side effects you experience. It is important to communicate openly with your doctor about your symptoms to determine the most appropriate dose for you. Meperidine has the potential to be habit-forming, so do not take larger doses, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than prescribed. If you have been using meperidine for more than a few weeks, do not stop taking it abruptly without consulting your doctor, as this may lead to withdrawal symptoms. Your doctor will likely reduce your dose gradually to prevent withdrawal. Symptoms of withdrawal may include restlessness, watery eyes, nasal congestion, yawning, sweating, chills, muscle pain, irritability, nervousness, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, diarrhea, rapid breathing, fast heartbeat, and back pain. Meperidine may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information if needed. Before taking meperidine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to meperidine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Be sure to mention specific medications such as acyclovir, antidepressants, butorphanol, cimetidine, chlorpromazine, fluphenazine, medications for anxiety or mental illness, muscle relaxants, pentazocine, perphenazine, phenytoin, prochlorperazine, ritonavir, sedatives, sleeping pills, thioridazine, trifluoperazine, trifluopromazine, and tranquilizers. Additionally, inform your doctor if you are taking or have recently stopped taking monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors, such as isocarboxazid, phenelzine, selegiline, or tranylcypromine, as these can interact with meperidine. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Inform your doctor if you use or have used street drugs, consume or have consumed large amounts of alcohol, or have recently undergone surgery. Also, disclose if you have or have had conditions such as Addison's disease, head injuries, brain pressure issues, mental illness, asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), sickle cell anemia, pheochromocytoma, spinal abnormalities affecting breathing, enlarged prostate, urethral stricture, irregular heartbeat, seizures, stomach problems, or thyroid, liver, kidney, or lung disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking meperidine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your surgeon or dentist that you are taking meperidine. Meperidine may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Discuss the safe use of alcohol with your doctor, as alcohol and street drugs can exacerbate meperidine's side effects and lead to serious harm or death. Be aware that meperidine may cause dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting when standing up too quickly, especially when starting the medication. To minimize this risk, rise slowly from a lying position and rest your feet on the floor for a few minutes before standing. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while taking meperidine. If you miss a dose and are taking meperidine regularly, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Meperidine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include lightheadedness, dizziness, weakness, headache, extreme calm, mood changes, confusion, agitation, upset stomach, vomiting, stomach pain or cramps, constipation, dry mouth, flushing, sweating, and changes in vision. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though uncommon, require immediate medical attention. These include slow or difficult breathing, uncontrollable shaking, muscle twitching or stiffness, seizures, hallucinations, slow, fast, or pounding heartbeat, difficulty urinating, fainting, rash, or hives. If you experience any unusual problems while taking meperidine, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store meperidine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture, and protect it from theft. Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication by flushing it down the toilet. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal instructions. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include slowed breathing, extreme drowsiness, coma, floppy muscles, cold and clammy skin, slow heartbeat, nausea, blurred vision, dizziness, and fainting. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking meperidine. Do not share this medication with others, as it is illegal and potentially dangerous. Consult your pharmacist with any questions about refilling your prescription.
